articles.title: ActivityPub Won by Being Boring

This allows independent networks to agree on their own shape and structure, making it possible for services like Mastodon, PeerTube, and Lemmy to share a social graph without becoming a single product. The protocol's plainness is a deliberate design choice, making it easy to implement and understand, and its simplicity allows for a robust and scalable architecture.

articles.title: There Is Still No Silver Bullet
articles.summary: The concept of software engineering has evolved over the years, with the essence of building software being the conceptual construct of its interlocking concepts, data, and relationships. This is a hard part of building software, according to Fred Brooks, who believes it is the specification, design, and testing of this conceptual construct, not the labor of representing it. This idea is supported by Peter Naur's theory of the program, which suggests that the shared mental model that the source code only partially represents is the key to building software. Brooks' prediction that a tool can only compress the accident, or the labor of representing, is a prediction that has never been wrong, and it highlights the importance of understanding the essence of software engineering.

articles.title: Let's not call it "tech debt," it's just "mess"
articles.summary: A few months ago I wrote about one of my methods for dealing with "technical debt" which is often misused as a metaphor for something more like "mess". This is a common enough usage that even when it's used correctly, people who aren't software developers but work with software developers often hear "mess", and they'll start to develop the impression that "tech debt" is something that developers say when they did their job poorly. The problem with this metaphor is that businesses like debt, there's such a thing as "the right amount" of debt for a business which can be predictable and controlled, whereas financial debt is unpredictable and uncontrollable.

articles.title: Moving integer division to floating-point is trivial
articles.summary: Moving integer division to floating-point is trivial because the math is straightforward and the implementation is easy. The claim is that for two integers x and y that fit in 53/24 bits for double/single precision, the floating-point division will yield the same integer result as integer division. This is achieved by setting rounding mode to TOWARD_ZERO and then back once done, but hitting control words is often expensive. The floating-point precision places the upper bound on integer width, and examples show that smaller widths can be handled trivially, such as 32-bit integers in doubles and 16-bit integers in singles.
